title: The Gift of the Magi
sourceTitle: O. Henry, "The Gift of the Magi" (1905), retold

scenes.title: A Dollar Eighty-Seven
scenes.narration: One dollar and eighty-seven cents. That was all she had in the world. Della counted it three times. And tomorrow would be Christmas.

scenes.title: Eight Dollars a Week
scenes.narration: A tiny New York flat, eight dollars a week. Jim and Della had almost nothing. Just two treasures.

scenes.title: Two Treasures
scenes.narration: One was Jim's gold watch, his grandfather's. The other was Della's hair. Let down, it rippled below her knees.

scenes.title: Hair Goods of All Kinds
scenes.narration: On went her old brown jacket. On went her old brown hat. Madame Sofronie: Hair Goods of All Kinds. "Twenty dollars," said Madame. "Give it to me quick," said Della.

scenes.title: The Platinum Chain
scenes.narration: For two hours, she ransacked the stores. Then she found it: a platinum fob chain. It cost twenty-one dollars. She ran home with eighty-seven cents.

scenes.title: Seven O'Clock
scenes.narration: She curled what was left. She looked like a truant schoolboy. At seven, she heard Jim on the stairs. "Please God, let him think I'm still pretty."

scenes.title: The Door
scenes.narration: The door opened. Jim stopped, and stared at her. It wasn't anger. It wasn't surprise. It was a look she could not read.

scenes.title: The Combs
scenes.narration: "I sold my hair to buy you a present." "My hair grows awfully fast, Jim." His gift was the jeweled combs she adored. And now, her hair was gone.

scenes.title: I Sold the Watch
scenes.narration: "Isn't it a dandy, Jim?" "Give me your watch, I want to see it on." Jim tumbled down on the couch, and smiled. "Dell," he said. "I sold the watch to buy your combs."

scenes.title: Two Foolish Children
scenes.narration: They held each other, laughing and crying. Two foolish children in a tiny flat. Each gave away their greatest treasure. For the other.

scenes.title: They Are the Magi
scenes.narration: The magi brought the first Christmas gifts. Of all who give gifts, these two were wisest. They are the magi.
